Staff reading this section are responsible for applying it without delay and for protecting animal welfare, passenger readiness, and clear service handling at every stage. Companion Animal Travel Desk Procedures. This section directs staff in the handling, review, and onward coordination of companion animal travel requests so that care remains consistent, calm, and fully traceable.

All requests must be checked against the travel file before any acceptance is confirmed. Staff must speak in plain words, give only the guidance needed for the case, and keep the tone steady even when the traveler is anxious. The welfare coordinator reviews comfort needs and any limits on crate use, feeding, or movement, and the welcome team prepares passengers for boarding with firm, respectful instructions. If a traveler arrives with more than one animal, each case must be handled separately so that no document, label, or service note is confused.

If the pet lounge is needed, the desk must confirm access through the proper channel before the traveler is sent onward. <<FACT F002>> Staff must never promise lounge use before the review is complete, and they must not imply approval where none has been issued. Any unusual condition, refusal, or concern must be recorded in the service log at once and passed without delay to the next responsible station.

Where quarantine handling is required, the desk must verify the routing notes, keep the traveler informed in clear language, and ensure that welfare steps are not skipped. <<FACT F027>> In such cases, staff must maintain strict control of labels, carrier checks, and handoff notes, and must not release an animal until the confirmed process is complete. If a traveler such as Sana Bianchi or Marcus Davis seeks guidance, the reply must remain concise, kind, and actionable, with no extra detail that could mislead or slow the process.

Report any uncertainty, delay, or welfare concern to the supervising coordinator or the duty manager at once. Companion Animal Travel Desk
